primary_claim: A Claude-4-Sonnet-based misalignment classifier, calibrated to a 0.1% positive rate on a synthetic 'ordinary' deployment distribution, shows highly variable approximate recall (0% to 85%) across different misalignment example sources -- notably only 7% recall on METR's real on-policy reward-hacking examples and low recall on subtle 'covered reasoning' model organisms -- illustrating why misalignment classifiers, unlike control monitors, cannot be rigorously adversarially evaluated, since 'intentionally misaligned trajectory' is not a crisp abstraction

effect.metric: approximate recall (TPR) at a 0.1% ordinary positive rate, across misalignment example sources
effect.value: recall varies from 0% to 85% depending on setting; 7% recall on METR's real on-policy reward-hacking examples; low recall on subtle 'covered reasoning' and code-sabotage model organisms; up to 85% recall on 'instrumental reasoning' model organisms

stated_future_work: significantly optimise the classifier (e.g. by providing labeled examples, clearer positive/negative specifications, or finetuning)
exhaustively cover more model organisms (behavioral specifications and procedures)
increase the size of the ordinary positive-rate dataset (e.g. 10x) and the resolution of classifier scores to reduce threshold variance
gather a wider range of in-the-wild and adversarial on-policy misalignment examples for future evaluations
explore rescuing adversarial evaluation by constraining to intentionally misaligned finetuned model organisms, or restricting red-teams to clear-cut, expert-agreed cases
limitations_stated: did not significantly optimise the classifier prompt/method
did not exhaustively cover all model organisms (behavioral specifications or procedures)
only 3 positive labels at the 0.1% ordinary positive rate, adding significant variance to threshold and recall estimates
ordinary dataset mixture was chosen somewhat arbitrarily and significantly affects thresholds/detection rates
only created three model organisms (off-policy procedures), and ambiguity in human labelling complicates precision estimation
quote: our early findings show that synthetic recall rates at 0.1% ordinary positive rate vary broadly, from 0% to 85%.
